AST-SYNTAX-ERROR.title: Syntax Error
AST-SYNTAX-ERROR.explanation: The file contains Python syntax that cannot be parsed by the Python interpreter.
AST-SYNTAX-ERROR.why_it_matters: Syntax errors prevent the program from starting or being imported, causing immediate crashes.
AST-SYNTAX-ERROR.possible_impact: Total application failure when this module is invoked or loaded at runtime.
AST-SYNTAX-ERROR.recommendation: Review the indicated line for unmatched brackets, missing colons, invalid keywords, or indentation issues.

AST-MUTABLE-DEFAULT.title: Mutable Default Argument in Function
AST-MUTABLE-DEFAULT.explanation: A function definition uses a mutable object (such as a list, dictionary, or set) as a default parameter value.
AST-MUTABLE-DEFAULT.why_it_matters: Default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined, not each time it is called. Any mutations persist across calls.
AST-MUTABLE-DEFAULT.possible_impact: Subsequent function calls unexpectedly share and accumulate modified state, causing non-deterministic logical bugs.
AST-MUTABLE-DEFAULT.recommendation: Set the default value to None, and initialize a new empty container inside the function body if the argument is None.

AST-BARE-EXCEPT.title: Bare 'except:' Clause
AST-BARE-EXCEPT.explanation: An except block catches all exceptions without specifying an exception class.
AST-BARE-EXCEPT.why_it_matters: A bare except catches SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt (Ctrl+C), and memory errors in addition to standard exceptions.
AST-BARE-EXCEPT.possible_impact: Prevents normal application termination, hides syntax or typo errors, and complicates debugging.
AST-BARE-EXCEPT.recommendation: Specify the exact exception class you expect (e.g. `except ValueError:`) or at minimum use `except Exception:`.

AST-BROAD-EXCEPTION.title: Catching BaseException Directly
AST-BROAD-EXCEPTION.explanation: An exception handler catches BaseException directly.
AST-BROAD-EXCEPTION.why_it_matters: BaseException is the root of all exceptions including critical system signals like KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit.
AST-BROAD-EXCEPTION.possible_impact: Interrupts normal signal handling and prevents graceful system shutdown.
AST-BROAD-EXCEPTION.recommendation: Catch `Exception` instead of `BaseException` to handle standard application runtime errors.

AST-DUPLICATE-DICT-KEY.title: Duplicate Dictionary Key
AST-DUPLICATE-DICT-KEY.explanation: A dictionary literal defines the same key more than once.
AST-DUPLICATE-DICT-KEY.why_it_matters: Python keeps only the last value assigned to duplicate keys, silently overwriting earlier values.
AST-DUPLICATE-DICT-KEY.possible_impact: Data loss in configuration or parameters, leading to unexpected runtime behaviour.
AST-DUPLICATE-DICT-KEY.recommendation: Remove or rename the duplicate key so each entry in the dictionary is distinct.

AST-SELF-ASSIGNMENT.title: Variable Self-Assignment
AST-SELF-ASSIGNMENT.explanation: A variable is assigned to itself (e.g., `x = x`).
AST-SELF-ASSIGNMENT.why_it_matters: Self-assignment does nothing useful and almost always indicates an incomplete edit, copy-paste mistake, or missing logic.
AST-SELF-ASSIGNMENT.possible_impact: Intended state change is never applied, causing silent algorithmic flaws.
AST-SELF-ASSIGNMENT.recommendation: Inspect what value was intended to be assigned, or remove the redundant assignment.

AST-UNREACHABLE-CODE.title: Unreachable Dead Code
AST-UNREACHABLE-CODE.explanation: Statements exist immediately after a terminal control statement (return, raise, break, or continue).
AST-UNREACHABLE-CODE.why_it_matters: The Python interpreter will never execute these statements under any circumstance.
AST-UNREACHABLE-CODE.possible_impact: Creates confusion for maintainers and hides code that was expected to run.
AST-UNREACHABLE-CODE.recommendation: Move the code above the return/raise statement if it must execute, or delete it entirely.

RUFF-F821.title: Undefined Variable or Name
RUFF-F821.explanation: A variable or function is referenced before it has been defined or imported in this scope.
RUFF-F821.why_it_matters: Referencing an unknown name triggers a NameError at runtime as soon as that execution path is reached.
RUFF-F821.possible_impact: Immediate NameError crash when this function or statement is called.
RUFF-F821.recommendation: Check for typos in the variable name, ensure it is defined before use, or add the missing import.

RUFF-F401.title: Unused Import Statement
RUFF-F401.explanation: A module or symbol is imported but never referenced anywhere in the file.
RUFF-F401.why_it_matters: Unused imports clutter the namespace, increase startup time, and can mask dependencies.
RUFF-F401.possible_impact: Slower module import time and reduced codebase readability.
RUFF-F401.recommendation: Remove the unused import statement or use the imported symbol.

RUFF-F841.title: Unused Local Variable
RUFF-F841.explanation: A local variable is assigned a value but its value is never subsequently read or used.
RUFF-F841.why_it_matters: Often indicates an incomplete implementation, unnecessary computation, or a typo in a subsequent reference.
RUFF-F841.recommendation: Use the variable, prefix it with an underscore (e.g., `_result`) if deliberately unused, or delete the assignment.

RUFF-E999.title: Syntax Error Detected by Linter
RUFF-E999.explanation: The file failed linter syntax parsing due to invalid Python grammar.
RUFF-E999.why_it_matters: Source code cannot be executed or compiled.
RUFF-E999.possible_impact: Module crash on import or execution.
RUFF-E999.recommendation: Correct the syntax error at the indicated file location.

JS-CONSOLE-LOG.title: Leftover Console Log Statement
JS-CONSOLE-LOG.explanation: A console.log/debug statement was left in the JavaScript/TypeScript source code.
JS-CONSOLE-LOG.why_it_matters: Production console statements clutter browser logs and can inadvertently leak internal state or data.
JS-CONSOLE-LOG.possible_impact: Minor performance overhead and unintended visibility of debug information.
JS-CONSOLE-LOG.recommendation: Remove console statements before deploying or use a proper logging framework with log levels.

JS-LOOSE-EQUALITY.title: Loose Equality Operator (==)
JS-LOOSE-EQUALITY.explanation: Comparison uses loose equality (`==` or `!=`) instead of strict equality (`===` or `!==`).
JS-LOOSE-EQUALITY.why_it_matters: JavaScript's loose equality performs implicit type coercion, leading to counter-intuitive equality results (e.g. `0 == ''` is true).
JS-LOOSE-EQUALITY.possible_impact: Edge cases in conditional checks fail unexpectedly, causing subtle runtime bugs.
JS-LOOSE-EQUALITY.recommendation: Replace `==` with `===` and `!=` with `!==` to ensure strict type and value matching.

JS-LOOSE-INEQUALITY.title: Loose Inequality Operator (!=)
JS-LOOSE-INEQUALITY.explanation: Comparison uses loose inequality (`!=`) instead of strict inequality (`!==`).
JS-LOOSE-INEQUALITY.why_it_matters: Implicit type coercion occurs prior to comparison, producing surprising evaluation results.
JS-LOOSE-INEQUALITY.possible_impact: Incorrect branch execution when comparing values of differing types.

JS-VAR-USAGE.title: Legacy 'var' Declaration
JS-VAR-USAGE.explanation: Variable is declared using the legacy `var` keyword.
JS-VAR-USAGE.why_it_matters: `var` is function-scoped and hoisted, which frequently causes scope leakage bugs in loops and blocks.
JS-VAR-USAGE.possible_impact: Accidental variable shadowing or overwriting across block scopes.
JS-VAR-USAGE.recommendation: Replace `var` with `const` for immutable bindings or `let` for variables that are reassigned.

JS-EMPTY-CATCH.title: Empty Catch Block
JS-EMPTY-CATCH.explanation: A try-catch block catches an exception but the catch block contains no statements.
JS-EMPTY-CATCH.why_it_matters: Exceptions are swallowed silently without logging, recovery, or alerting the user.
JS-EMPTY-CATCH.possible_impact: Critical failures remain completely invisible, leaving the program in a corrupted state.
JS-EMPTY-CATCH.recommendation: Log the error, rethrow it, or add graceful recovery logic inside the catch block.

JS-DEBUGGER-STATEMENT.title: Debugger Statement in Code
JS-DEBUGGER-STATEMENT.explanation: A `debugger;` statement was left in the code.
JS-DEBUGGER-STATEMENT.why_it_matters: If developer tools are open in a user's browser, execution pauses abruptly.
JS-DEBUGGER-STATEMENT.possible_impact: Freezes user interface and breaks production user experience.
JS-DEBUGGER-STATEMENT.recommendation: Remove `debugger;` statements prior to committing or deploying.

JS-ALERT-STATEMENT.title: Blocking Alert Dialog
JS-ALERT-STATEMENT.why_it_matters: Alert modals block the browser thread and provide poor user experience.
JS-ALERT-STATEMENT.possible_impact: Freezes JavaScript execution until the user manually dismisses the dialog.
JS-ALERT-STATEMENT.recommendation: Use non-blocking UI notifications or modals instead of native `alert()`.

SEC-HARDCODED-SECRET.title: Hardcoded Secret or API Key
SEC-HARDCODED-SECRET.explanation: A sensitive credential, API key, password, or authentication token was found hardcoded in source code.
SEC-HARDCODED-SECRET.why_it_matters: Committed credentials can be extracted by anyone with read access to the repository or binaries.
SEC-HARDCODED-SECRET.possible_impact: Complete compromise of backend services, external APIs, or user data if repository is exposed.
SEC-HARDCODED-SECRET.recommendation: Move secrets to external environment variables (e.g. .env) and use a secrets management service. Rotate any exposed keys immediately.

SEC-AWS-CREDENTIAL.title: Hardcoded AWS Access Key
SEC-AWS-CREDENTIAL.explanation: An AWS Access Key ID or Secret Key pattern was detected in the file.
SEC-AWS-CREDENTIAL.why_it_matters: AWS credentials grant access to cloud infrastructure, databases, and compute instances.
SEC-AWS-CREDENTIAL.possible_impact: Unauthorized access to cloud infrastructure, data theft, and extreme unexpected cloud billing.
SEC-AWS-CREDENTIAL.recommendation: Revoke and rotate the exposed AWS key immediately in IAM. Use IAM Roles or AWS Secrets Manager.

SEC-GITHUB-TOKEN.title: Hardcoded GitHub Personal Access Token
SEC-GITHUB-TOKEN.explanation: A GitHub Personal Access Token (`ghp_...`) was found in plaintext in the codebase.
SEC-GITHUB-TOKEN.why_it_matters: GitHub tokens can grant write and administration access to your repositories and organizations.
SEC-GITHUB-TOKEN.possible_impact: Repository tampering, unauthorized code commits, and exposure of private source code.
SEC-GITHUB-TOKEN.recommendation: Revoke the token immediately via GitHub Developer Settings and configure secret scanning.

SEC-SQL-INJECTION.title: Potential SQL Injection via Dynamic String
SEC-SQL-INJECTION.explanation: A database query is constructed dynamically using an f-string or string concatenation.
SEC-SQL-INJECTION.why_it_matters: Unsanitized input concatenated into SQL queries allows attackers to alter query logic.
SEC-SQL-INJECTION.possible_impact: Data exfiltration, unauthorized database modifications, bypassing authentication, or database deletion.
SEC-SQL-INJECTION.recommendation: Use parameterized queries (e.g., `cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s', (user_id,))`) or an ORM.

SEC-SQLI-CONCAT.title: SQL Query String Concatenation
SEC-SQLI-CONCAT.explanation: Raw SQL query commands are concatenated with string variables.
SEC-SQLI-CONCAT.why_it_matters: Direct string concatenation bypasses SQL sanitization boundaries.
SEC-SQLI-CONCAT.possible_impact: SQL injection leading to unauthorized database access.
SEC-SQLI-CONCAT.recommendation: Switch to parameterized queries or prepared statements.

SEC-OS-SYSTEM.title: Use of os.system()
SEC-OS-SYSTEM.explanation: `os.system()` executes commands directly in the host shell.
SEC-OS-SYSTEM.why_it_matters: Shell execution is vulnerable to command injection if input contains shell metacharacters (`;`, `&`, `|`).
SEC-OS-SYSTEM.possible_impact: Arbitrary command execution on the host operating system.
SEC-OS-SYSTEM.recommendation: Use `subprocess.run(['command', 'arg1'], shell=False)` with arguments passed as an explicit list.

SEC-SUBPROCESS-SHELL.title: Subprocess with shell=True
SEC-SUBPROCESS-SHELL.why_it_matters: Enabling the shell parser allows an attacker to chain arbitrary shell commands.
SEC-SUBPROCESS-SHELL.possible_impact: Remote code execution on the underlying host server.
SEC-SUBPROCESS-SHELL.recommendation: Remove `shell=True` and pass command and arguments as a list of strings.

SEC-DYNAMIC-EXEC.title: Dangerous Dynamic Code Execution (eval/exec)
SEC-DYNAMIC-EXEC.explanation: The code uses `eval()` or `exec()` to dynamically execute Python code.
SEC-DYNAMIC-EXEC.why_it_matters: Evaluating untrusted strings executes arbitrary code with the permissions of the current process.
SEC-DYNAMIC-EXEC.possible_impact: Full application compromise and server takeover.
SEC-DYNAMIC-EXEC.recommendation: Avoid `eval()` and `exec()`. Use `ast.literal_eval()` for safely parsing literals, or JSON parsers for structured data.

SEC-WEAK-HASH.title: Weak Hashing Algorithm (MD5 / SHA1)
SEC-WEAK-HASH.explanation: The code uses MD5 or SHA1 cryptographic hash functions.
SEC-WEAK-HASH.why_it_matters: MD5 and SHA1 suffer from proven collision vulnerabilities and cannot safely verify integrity or secure passwords.
SEC-WEAK-HASH.possible_impact: Collision attacks, signature forgery, and rainbow-table attacks against stored hashes.
SEC-WEAK-HASH.recommendation: Use SHA-256 or SHA-3 for general hashing, or specialized algorithms like bcrypt/argon2 for password hashing.

SEC-WEAK-CIPHER.title: Weak or Deprecated Encryption Cipher
SEC-WEAK-CIPHER.explanation: The code references deprecated ciphers like DES, RC4, or Blowfish.
SEC-WEAK-CIPHER.why_it_matters: Legacy ciphers have known cryptanalytic weaknesses and small key sizes.
SEC-WEAK-CIPHER.possible_impact: Encrypted sensitive traffic or data can be decrypted by third parties.
SEC-WEAK-CIPHER.recommendation: Use AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 with modern cryptographic libraries (e.g. cryptography).

SEC-DEBUG-ENABLED.title: Debug Mode Enabled in Configuration
SEC-DEBUG-ENABLED.why_it_matters: Debug mode provides detailed stack traces, environment variables, and interactive consoles upon errors.
SEC-DEBUG-ENABLED.possible_impact: Exposure of sensitive environment keys and database internals to public web users.
SEC-DEBUG-ENABLED.recommendation: Set `DEBUG = False` in production, or read debug settings dynamically from an environment variable.

BANDIT-B602.title: Subprocess Call with shell=True
BANDIT-B602.explanation: Bandit detected a subprocess invocation with `shell=True`.
BANDIT-B602.why_it_matters: Allows shell command injection if any part of the command string is untrusted.
BANDIT-B602.possible_impact: Arbitrary command execution on the host machine.
BANDIT-B602.recommendation: Set `shell=False` and supply command arguments as an array.

BANDIT-B307.title: Use of Blacklisted eval()
BANDIT-B307.explanation: Bandit detected the use of Python's built-in `eval()` function.
BANDIT-B307.why_it_matters: `eval` executes arbitrary Python code strings at runtime.
BANDIT-B307.possible_impact: Remote code execution if user input reaches the eval call.
BANDIT-B307.recommendation: Refactor to use `ast.literal_eval()` or native dictionary lookups.

QUAL-HIGH-COMPLEXITY.title: Excessive Cyclomatic Complexity
QUAL-HIGH-COMPLEXITY.explanation: A function or method contains too many branching paths (if/for/while statements).
QUAL-HIGH-COMPLEXITY.why_it_matters: Functions with high cyclomatic complexity (> 10) are difficult to comprehend, maintain, and thoroughly unit test.
QUAL-HIGH-COMPLEXITY.possible_impact: Increased defect density, untested edge cases, and high maintenance costs.
QUAL-HIGH-COMPLEXITY.recommendation: Refactor the function by extracting smaller helper functions or applying polymorphism.

QUAL-LOW-MAINTAINABILITY.title: Low Maintainability Index
QUAL-LOW-MAINTAINABILITY.explanation: The file scored poorly on the Maintainability Index metric.
QUAL-LOW-MAINTAINABILITY.why_it_matters: Low maintainability indicates high code volume, complex branching, and low comment density.
QUAL-LOW-MAINTAINABILITY.possible_impact: High technical debt and increased time required to fix future bugs or add features.
QUAL-LOW-MAINTAINABILITY.recommendation: Break the file into smaller modules and simplify complex routines.

QUAL-DEEP-NESTING.title: Deeply Nested Control Blocks
QUAL-DEEP-NESTING.explanation: Control flow is nested 5 or more levels deep.
QUAL-DEEP-NESTING.why_it_matters: Deep nesting strains cognitive load, making it hard to track state and conditions.
QUAL-DEEP-NESTING.possible_impact: Subtle logic bugs and difficult-to-maintain code.
QUAL-DEEP-NESTING.recommendation: Use guard clauses (`return early`), invert condition checks, or extract inner logic into helper functions.

QUAL-FILE-TOO-LONG.title: Excessive File Length
QUAL-FILE-TOO-LONG.explanation: The file exceeds 500 lines of code.
QUAL-FILE-TOO-LONG.why_it_matters: Very large files typically violate the Single Responsibility Principle.
QUAL-FILE-TOO-LONG.possible_impact: High risk of merge conflicts and difficulty in code navigation.
QUAL-FILE-TOO-LONG.recommendation: Separate distinct classes or concerns into individual files.

QUAL-TODO-COMMENT.title: Unresolved TODO or FIXME Marker
QUAL-TODO-COMMENT.explanation: An unresolved reminder comment (TODO, FIXME, or HACK) was left in the code.
QUAL-TODO-COMMENT.why_it_matters: Indicates incomplete implementation or acknowledged technical debt.
QUAL-TODO-COMMENT.possible_impact: Known deficiencies may slip into production unnoticed.
QUAL-TODO-COMMENT.recommendation: Complete the required task and remove the reminder, or track it in your issue management system.
